To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) gene expression is influenced by the form and quantity of nitrogen fertilizer; (ii) specific genes are differentially expressed in the endosperm when wheat is grown with organic or mineral fertilizer; and (iii) these genes are involved in a variety of biological processes including nitrogen metabolism, storage protein biosynthesis and cell division.
the use of organic sources for nitrogen fertilization of wheat results in markedly different gene expression in the developing grain.
the form of nitrogen fertilizer applied to wheat has a significant impact on the expression of specific genes in the endosperm of the grain.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the use of molecular markers to identify and characterize genes involved in the nitrogen metabolism of plants, and in particular to determine the effects on gene expression of different sources and amounts of nitrogen fertilizer in field crops.
the effects of different nitrogen fertilizers on gene expression in wheat grain.
understanding the molecular basis of nitrogen use efficiency and the impact of nitrogenous fertilizer on the quality of wheat grain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
wheat grain protein content is higher when grown with inorganic nitrogen fertilizer than when grown with organic fertilizer.
wheat grain grown in organic systems is markedly different in its gene expression to wheat grown in conventional systems.

the use of different forms of nitrogen fertilizers has a significant effect on the gene expression profile of wheat and that this is most likely a consequence of the differential nitrogen metabolism that is required for the assimilation of the different forms of nitrogen fertilizer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gene expression in wheat grain is significantly influenced by both the amount and the form of nitrogen fertilizer and that these effects can be detected in the field.
the form of N fertilizer used has a profound effect on the gene expression in the grain.
the form of nitrogen fertilizer used by farmers can have profound effects at the level of specific gene expression in the grain of the crop.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gene expression is sensitive to the form of nitrogen fertilizer, and that this can be exploited to define the differences between organic and conventional agriculture.
the form of nitrogen fertilizer has a profound effect on gene expression in wheat.
the form of nitrogenous fertilizers can influence gene expression in wheat, and this may be a general phenomenon in other crops as well.
